billing.why: A retried charge takes the money twice and the second one is not a mistake anybody can see without reconciling the ledger.

webhooks.why: A provider retries until it gets a 2xx, so a handler that is not fenced applies the same subscription change on every retry.

tool-actions.why: A tool call replayed after a lost response sends the message, files the ticket or makes the commit a second time.

schedule-execution.why: A schedule that fires twice for one due time runs the work twice and tells the reader twice.

upload-finalize.why: Finalizing the same upload twice creates a second asset for one set of bytes and bills the storage twice.

external-writes.why: A generation request replayed against a provider is paid for twice and returns two different results for one prompt.

account-deletion.why: A second erasure of an account already erased must be a no-op rather than an error the caller retries forever.

provisioning.why: A directory sync that replays creates the member twice and the second one carries no grants.

invite-acceptance.why: Accepting the same invitation twice would seat the member twice and bill for both seats; the status transition is the fence and a second accept is refused as already used.
